with_model_outputs.label: D1 after a rewarded visit to S1
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO or D2), and only when the reward input is 1 and the previous trial reached S1. Its preconditions are the observed reward plus the observed reached state, so it is an S1-was-rewarded detector (the conjunction of state and reward, whatever action was taken, common or rare). (D1 & reward & prev_state==1) has precision 1.00 on dev. Its recall is only 0.78 because prev_state is undefined (-1) on the first trial of each window, even though the agent did see that state. For those trials only, the predicate uses the agent upcoming choice action==1 as a proxy; that is the only FUTURE variable used, and it is the agent own computed choice, not a random outcome. Dev scores: P 0.995, R 0.984, F1 0.989. Using prev_state != 2 with no future variable gives F1 0.90. It does not fire after an unrewarded trial or after a rewarded visit to S2. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 1.76, max 2.18); I did not check what modulates it.

issues: All the factual claims check out. The feature fires only at D1: GO and D2 have 0 active steps out of 380k each. Activity after unrewarded trials is negligible: 482 active steps at in_rew==0, with tiny activations such as 0.02.

(D1 & in_rew==1 & prev_state==1) has precision 1.00 on both dev and test, with recall 0.78/0.79. (D1 & in_rew==1 & prev_state==2) has precision 0, so the feature never fires after a rewarded visit to S2.

The feature fires regardless of action and transition. A rare-transition S1 reward (prev_common==0 or prev_action==2) still gives precision 1.0. When S2 is the good state, the S1-rewarded case still gives precision 1.0. When the upcoming action is a2 after a rewarded S1 visit, precision is 1.0. So within-window firing does not depend on the agent's upcoming choice, and the action==1 term is only a stand-in for the unseen prev_state on the window's first trial.

Residual errors are all at step 0 (rel -3), where prev_state is undefined and the proxy has to guess (2041 missed steps, 1.1% of activation mass; 686 false positives on test). This comes from the window boundary, not from the feature.

For that first-trial proxy, the observed-only alternative (good==1 instead of action==1) gives test F1 0.962, and the choice-logit proxy (choice>0) gives 0.985. Both are close to the recorded predicate's 0.989. So the label 'S1 was rewarded' rests on observed variables, and the future variable fills in only the window boundary, which the explanation already says.
